claims.summary: In the setting of cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction (X i.i.d. uniform, Y evenly spread, L>=132, cell-smeared measures on the grid of side 1/ceil(32/s), s=L sqrt(log N/N)), there is a universal L_0 such that for every L>=132, with probability tending to one the penalized discrepancy D_N is at least sqrt(N log N)/(4 L_0) for all alpha_1,alpha_2 in [1,infinity] simultaneously, endpoints included; more generally on the same event for every class of Lipschitz functions containing the 1-Lipschitz functions vanishing on the boundary (any separable penalty with nondecreasing phi_j, phi_j(1) <= 1).
claims.assessment: Working proof: 1-Lipschitz functions vanishing on the boundary lie in the class (psi*_alpha(1) <= 1, psi*_infinity(y) = y for y <= N); Theorem 4.6.1 of Talagrand's monograph with McDiarmid's inequality for the main term; the X-side smearing error is a sum of within-cell discrepancies, O(sqrt(N log log N)) in expectation by Theorem 4.5.3 at cell scale and Cauchy-Schwarz; the Y-side error is O(sqrt N) through the evenly spread rectangles meeting grid lines.
claims.rationale: Shows that the order sqrt(N log N) of conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy is forced at every pair, endpoints included, through the elementary Lipschitz baseline that lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound left unchecked; that lemma's contribution on the curve is therefore not the order.
claims.next_action: None for the order; the open question is the constant, conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy itself.
